markets._doc: Market squares in shop paint: spacing between squares, the square's width and depth, how near a street it must lie, the pull (score off) of a square's rim for shops, the open shop-paint cells a square waits for, the cells round a new square that open unpainted ground is painted for shops, the shops the town keeps per square before it grows another, and the score added to a shop off the streets (tiles).

closes._doc: Side lanes in home paint: once a day the open home paint at least 'deep' tiles from any street and within 'near' tiles of what's built gets a lane to the nearest street, 'perDay' at most.

tiers.name: Thorp
tiers.blurb: A charter, a wagon and a handful of settlers at the ford.

tiers.name: Hamlet
tiers.blurb: Enough hearths to call it a place. Quarries and sheepfolds can open.

tiers.name: Village
tiers.blurb: A market green and a grain store. New wards can grow round the old town, weavers and carpenters set up, and cottages grow into timber houses.

tiers.name: Town
tiers.blurb: A chartered market town. The Temple Ward and the riverside can grow beyond the old town's edge, stone walls can ring the old town, and land can be zoned medium density, where timber houses become stone townhouses.

tiers.name: Large Town
tiers.blurb: Magistrates, guild money and stone walls. Castle Hill and the Field Ward can grow, vineyards, scriptoria, theatres and libraries follow, and the crowded old town can be zoned high density, where tall houses rise wall to wall.

tiers.name: City
tiers.blurb: A walled city of many faiths and trades. Manors rise on Castle Hill, Gateside and Tanners' Row can grow, and the city can raise a cathedral, an arena and a keep.

tiers.name: Great City
tiers.blurb: A great city whose name is known in every court. Its wealth draws the best heroes and the worst enemies.

wards.name: Old Town
wards.blurb: The charter land around the hall, where the first families built.

wards.name: Market Ward
wards.blurb: Shops and stalls where the trade roads come in. Commercial land here sells dear.

wards.name: Trades Ward
wards.blurb: Workshops, yards and smoke. Cheap land for the crafts.

wards.name: Lamplit Quarter
wards.blurb: Violet lamps that never need oil, crooked towers and domed schools, grown up around the library and the hedge mages' workshops. Its scholars add to the library's lore.

wards.name: Temple Ward
wards.blurb: Quiet streets around the temples. The only ground holy enough for a cathedral.

wards.name: Castle Hill
wards.blurb: The best-kept streets in town. Manors and the keep can only rise here, and rents are steep.

wards.name: Riverside
wards.blurb: Wharves, fish sheds and boat-builders outside the walls. Fisheries can only work here.

wards.name: Field Ward
wards.blurb: Old caravan grounds outside the gates. Cheap, crowded and rowdy; tenements go up here.

wards.name: Gateside
wards.blurb: Caravan yards and coaching inns at the gate, where the trade roads come in.

wards.name: Tanners' Row
wards.blurb: Downwind and outside the walls: tanneries, dye pits and the poor who work them.

unsettled.name: the edge of town
unsettled.blurb: Open ground round the old town. Whatever is built here first decides what quarter it grows into.

unsettled.name: the outskirts
unsettled.blurb: Ground beyond the walls. Whatever is built here first decides what quarter it grows into.

densities.name: Low
densities.blurb: Cottages and timber houses with gardens and lanes between, as in any frontier village.

densities.name: Medium
densities.blurb: Houses may rise to three-storey stone townhouses, and manors on Castle Hill.

densities.name: High
densities.blurb: Tall houses of four and five storeys built wall to wall, the way a walled city's old core packs in. Crowded: residents grumble a little.
